questions.q: The decimal value of the binary number 111010 is:
Mail merge in MS Word is used to —
options: Merge two Word files into one
Join two tables side by side
Create many personalised documents from one template and a data list
questions.solution: **Mail merge** produces one finished copy per record — same letter body, different names and addresses.

questions.q: Downloading a large software file from the Internet should use —
questions.solution: A file must arrive complete and in order — **TCP's reliability** is worth its slowness.

questions.q: The default file extension of a workbook created in MS Excel 2019 is:
questions.solution: Excel 2007 onwards saves workbooks as .xlsx (Office Open XML). .xls is the 97-2003 format, .xlsm is macro-enabled, .ods is OpenDocument.
questions.shortcut: X = XML = 2007+ across all Office extensions.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: Possession needs **whose**, even for things: 'The building **whose** roof was damaged'. 'Which roof' would mean 'choose a roof' — a different sentence entirely.
questions.shortcut: whose = of which; which roof ≠ whose roof.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

A disease that spreads over many countries and the whole world
questions.solution: pan = all → world-wide spread = **pandemic**. An epidemic spreads fast but stays within one area; endemic is always present in one area; quarantine is a period of isolation, not a disease word.

questions.q: Select the correct plural of 'analysis'.
questions.solution: **analyses** — nouns in -is change to -es in the plural (crisis -> crises, thesis -> theses). 'analysis' is the singular, and the other forms do not exist.

questions.q: Three parts of a sentence are given in order, followed by a fourth option. If there is no error anywhere, select 'No error'.
questions.solution: **Hardly** means 'almost not' — the intended meaning needs the adverb of effort **hard**: 'working hard since morning'. The perfect form in parts 1 and 3 is correct.
questions.shortcut: hardly = almost never; hard = with effort.

questions.q: In Sufi practice, the musical recital of devotion is called —
questions.solution: **Sama** is the musical recital (root of qawwali); **zikr** is silent/chanted remembrance; **silsila** is the order's chain.

questions.q: The **Hoysala** capital **Dorasamudra** is today known as —
questions.solution: Dorasamudra is modern **Halebidu** (Karnataka); the Hoysaleswara temple stands there, and Belur's Chennakeshava temple is nearby.

questions.q: The fjord coast, carved by glaciers into deep sea inlets, is a typical feature of:
questions.solution: **Norway's** west coast is the classic land of **fjords**. The Volga is Europe's longest river; the Danube crosses the most countries.

questions.q: Which one of the sixteen mahajanapadas lay **south of the Vindhyas**?
questions.solution: **Assaka (Ashmaka)**, on the Godavari with capital Potana (Potali), was the only mahajanapada south of the Vindhyas. Avanti (Malwa) is north of the range.
questions.shortcut: South = the odd southern one, Assaka.

questions.q: From a point $15$ m from the base of a flagstaff, the elevation of its top is $60^\circ$. The height of the flagstaff is:
questions.shortcut: 60° → height = √3 × distance. Trap: $5\sqrt3$ — that is the distance rule inverted.

questions.q: The supplement of an angle is three times its complement. The angle is:

Revenue of firm A (in ₹ crore):

| Year | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 80 | 96 | 120 | 144 |

The percentage growth in revenue from 2021 to 2022 is:
The value of $\tan^2 75^\circ + \tan^2 15^\circ$ is:
Arrange as in a dictionary: **Judge, Judo, Joust, Journal, Jostle.** Which word is **second from the right**?
questions.solution: 2nd letters: o (Jostle, Journal, Joust) vs u (Judge, Judo); o < u → the o-group comes first. 3rd letters: s (Jostle) vs u (Journal, Joust) → Jostle first. 4th letters: r (Journal) vs s (Joust) → Journal, Joust. Full order: Jostle, Journal, Joust, Judge, Judo → slot 5 + 1 − 2 = 4 → **Judge**.
questions.shortcut: The 2nd letter splits J-o... before J-u... — check column two before assuming a shared stem.

questions.q:
**Statement:** The price of a notebook rose from ₹40 to ₹50, while the price of a pen rose from ₹10 to ₹15.

**Conclusions:**
I. The price of the notebook rose by a larger percentage than the price of the pen.
II. The price of the pen rose by 50%.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: Notebook: (50 − 40)/40 = 25%. Pen: (15 − 10)/10 = 50%. I claims 25% > 50% — false, **does not follow** (a bigger rupee rise is not a bigger percentage rise). II is exactly 50% — **follows**. Answer: **Only II**.
questions.shortcut: Compare percentages on the base, not the rupee jump.

questions.q: Two different positions of the same dice are shown. Which letter is on the face opposite to **I**? (Ignore the orientation of the letters/numbers.)
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 124 59" width="124" height="59" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.3" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><polygon points="4,21 38,21 38,55 4,55"/><polygon points="4,21 38,21 55,4 21,4"/><polygon points="38,21 55,4 55,38 38,55"/><text x="21" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">H</text><text x="29.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">J</text><text x="46.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">I</text><polygon points="69,21 103,21 103,55 69,55"/><polygon points="69,21 103,21 120,4 86,4"/><polygon points="103,21 120,4 120,38 103,55"/><text x="86" y="43" font-size="14" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">J</text><text x="94.5" y="16.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">H</text><text x="111.5" y="33.5" font-size="10" text-anchor="middle" fill="currentColor" stroke="none" font-family="sans-serif">L</text></svg>
questions.solution: The two views share **H** and **J** — two common faces, so each of them touches the other faces shown. The face left over in the first view (**I**) and the face left over in the second (**L**) must therefore be opposite each other.
questions.shortcut: Two common faces in two views: the leftovers are opposite.

questions.q:
**Statement:** Advertisement: 'Fresh vegetables delivered to your door within 30 minutes — order on our app!'

**Assumptions:**
I. Some people want fresh vegetables delivered quickly.
II. Some people are able to place orders through a mobile app.

Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
options: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.solution: Negate I: nobody wants quick delivery — the advert's hook is useless, so I is **implicit**. Negate II: nobody can order through an app — no one can respond, so II is **implicit**. Answer: **both**.
questions.shortcut: An advert assumes its hook attracts someone and that someone can respond.
